season_source: https://www.goldenbellccc.org/_files/ugd/ccbdfd_9b22053942c54a46a558186a78b0f11d.pdf (footer 'May - September / 719.687.9561 / www.goldenbellccc.org'), read 2026-10-27. The stored year_round: true rested on note prose only.
note: Church camp (Colorado District Church of the Nazarene) in the forested foothills at the base of Pikes Peak, ~9,180 ft, with an RV park sold to the public by the night. No alcohol or marijuana on camp property. Heated indoor pool (no lifeguard), mini golf, disc golf, catch-and-release fishing, camp hiking trails. --Claude

name: Haggard's RV Campground

season.note: Closes for the winter on October 31; the opening date is not posted.

season_source: https://haggardsrvcampground.com/ ('Taking daily/weekly reservations/close for the Winter Season Oct. 31st'), read 2026-10-27
note: Transient RV park on US-50 between Pueblo and Canon City (~mile marker 298), in open prairie with mountain views. Unheated pool (Memorial Day - Labor Day, weather permitting). The well water is high in iron and minerals: bring an RV water filter and bottled drinking water. --Claude

name: Gremlin Cove
season_source: note prose
note: USACE Harlan County Lake park at the east end of the lake by the dam, just east of North Shore Marina, Republican City. Basic undesignated camping: pick a spot with a fire ring and picnic table among the trees; pay at the self-pay vault. Restrooms, playground and a reservable group shelter. Corps office 308-799-2105. --Claude

name: Hunter Cove

season.note: Reservable May 1 - September 30; first come, first served in April and October-November (walk-in electric $20).

season_source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233517/rates ('First-come, First-served Season' 2026-04-01..04-30 and 2026-10-01..11-30 alongside the May-September Peak Season), read 2026-11-04
note: USACE park at the east end of Harlan County Lake near Republican City. Two loops (HCOV and HCOV N); the south row of the main loop sits on the open lakeshore above the riprap. Paved main road, gravel loops. Playground, volleyball court, boat ramp and fish-cleaning station; two marinas on the east end. Attendant on duty May-September; all campers check in on arrival. --Claude

name: South Outlet
season_source: note prose
note: USACE Harlan County Lake: primitive grass camping below the dam's south outlet, near Republican City; sites marked by a picnic table and fire ring. Drive-in via washboard gravel; access road is narrow if meeting boat trailers, but RV-usable (firsthand RV reviews). --Claude

name: Bancroft Municipal Park
season_source: note prose
note: Village of Bancroft municipal park on the village's SW/NW edge; ~5 drive-in electric+water sites (camping NW of the park off Public Rd) on open flat grass -- ample room for a 23-ft Class C. RV dump and flush toilets on site; no showers noted. Open May-Oct, roughly $6/night, very cheap. Not on recreation.gov -- book/inquire by phone via Ru-Des Mini Mart; effectively FCFS/call-ahead. RV Life unrated (0 star, price $). --Claude

name: Beck Memorial Park
season_source: note prose
note: Village of Decatur park on the Missouri River at the edge of town (lower camping area along the river, upper loop by the ballfields); boat ramp and fish-cleaning station. A 2021 reviewer found it full of long-term campers who 'book for a couple months at a time', so call ahead in season. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night (RV Life review, October 2025). --Claude

name: Humboldt Lake Park
season_source: note prose
note: City of Humboldt lake park on the south side of town, with two small fishing ponds, a walking trail and ball fields. Grass sites, reported level. Reserve and prepay through the city office by phone or email (Humboldt.clerk@gmail.com). Max vehicle length 25 ft (reported by VisitNebraska, not on the city page), so a 23-ft rig fits with little margin; a motorhome camped in site 3 in May 2026. Trains run on the line along the south edge. --Claude

name: Lynch RV Park
season_source: note prose
note: Village of Lynch RV park on the south side of town (4th St & Railroad Ave), a short walk from the main street; Ponca Creek is beyond the trees to the south-east. Back-in gravel pads in grass with tables and fire pits, a covered picnic area. Pay at a bar downtown or call for pickup; no reservations. Grass can be long and neighbouring dogs noisy (2024 review). CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $25 a night in July 2024 (The Dyrt and Campendium reviews); the village has no web page (2026-11-05). --Claude

name: Newman Grove City Park
season_source: note prose
note: City-run campground in Newman Grove's town park, with a few partial-hookup sites besides the full-hookup ones; pool, playground and a walking/bike path next to it. Pay on the honor system at the City Hall drop box. A May 2026 camper found it muddy, rutted and weedy. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $20 a night in July 2026 (RV Life review); the city's recreation page could not be read. --Claude

name: Schuyler City Campground
season_source: note prose
note: City of Schuyler municipal campground, ~1 mi S of US-30/Hwy-15 jct on E side of Hwy 15. 35 RV sites (RV-only, no tent), electric hookups (35-amp per most listings; a few 20-amp), water at most sites, dump station, flush toilets, pay showers, playground; adjacent day-use park, golf course, and stocked fishing ponds. Open Apr-Oct. FCFS, no online reservations; pay on site ($10 primitive / $15 electric / $20 full hookup). Loop layout fits a 23-ft Class C with room for larger rigs. --Claude

name: Stuart Municipal Park
season_source: note prose
note: City of Stuart municipal park on the Cowboy Trail. ~20 RV sites with electric + water, 30-amp; dump station, restrooms, showers, drinking water, playground. Rigs to ~35 ft. Season ~March-Nov. FCFS, no reservations; cheap town-park rate. Tent camping free. --Claude

name: Eagle Canyon Hideaway
season_source: https://www.campspot.com/park/eagle-canyon-hideaway (no site types offered on 2026-10-20 or 2027-01-26, while June 2027 sells), read 2026-10-13; replaces the note scan's {"year_round": true}
note: In a canyon draw near the south shore of Lake McConaughy, with log cabins too.  Marketed as near the lake, but reviewers say the water is well off and not walkable when the lake is low. --Claude

name: Fishberry Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Private RV park on US-83 about 5 mi north of Valentine (90440 US Hwy 83), in the Sandhills near the Niobrara. 22 full-hookup pull-throughs (most 50-amp), 80-100 ft, on gravel; bathrooms/showers, picnic pavilion. Regular season May-October. --Claude

name: Green Valley State Park

season.note: No page gives campground dates. Iowa DNR publishes off-season camping rates (Oct 16 - Apr 30) and its 2026 alert closes the park to camping Nov 6-9, so camping continues past October.

season_source: Stored Apr 1-Oct 31 came from note prose. https://www.iowadnr.gov/media/6743/download (off-season rates Oct 16 - Apr 30) + https://programs.iowadnr.gov/parkforms/pages/ViewParkAlerts ('closed for camping ... November 6th through ... November 9th'), read 2026-11-02
note: Iowa DNR reservoir park on Green Valley Lake NW of Creston, with buddy and group sites and 3 camping cabins; paved roads, gravel pads. Lake-side RV pads are 20-21 and 28-30; other RV sites sit inland of the loop road. --Claude

name: Buck Creek (Rathbun Lake)
season_source: note prose
note: USACE Rathbun Lake campground on a point in three loops (A, B, F), open grassy areas dotted with trees. Open ~May 8-Sep 29. --Claude

name: Prairie Ridge B Area (Rathbun Lake)

season.note: Campground season May - September; closed October - April (USACE). Rates run May 15 - September 14.

season_source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233593 (facility_phone: 'FOR CAMPGROUND INQUIRIES DURING MAY-SEPTEMBER PLEASE CALL 641-724-3103. DURING CLOSED SEASON OCTOBER-APRIL PLEASE CALL 641-647-2464') + rates (Peak Season 2026-05-15 to 2026-09-14), read 2026-11-03
note: USACE Rathbun Lake campground on a high prairie ridge between Buck Creek and Honey Creek, SW of Moravia; the last 2.5 miles in are gravel (200th Avenue). Woodland draws and timbered hillsides, a modern playground, and a boat ramp sheltered on three sides with a courtesy dock and fish-cleaning station. An 8-mile trail links to Honey Creek Resort. Unstaffed. --Claude

name: Shady Creek (Mississippi River)

season.note: rec.gov sells nights May 1 - October 24 in 2026 (through the fourth Saturday of October; the 2027 table runs May 1 - October 23).

season_source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233624/rates (Peak Season 2026-05-01 to 2026-10-24, 2027-05-01 to 2027-10-23), read 2026-11-03
note: USACE Rock Island District campground on the Iowa bank of the Mississippi between Davenport and Muscatine, a 22-acre wooded park with a boat ramp, playground, nature trail and shore fishing; Wildcat Den State Park is just north. --Claude

name: Adair City Park Campground

season.note: Closes during freezing temperatures, approximately November-April; the bathhouse and restrooms are locked in winter, though hydrants, electricity and the dump station are listed as available year-round (contact City Hall about conditions).

season_source: https://adairia.gov/camping/ ('The campground closes during freezing temperatures, approximately November–April. Bathhouse and restrooms are locked during winter months. Hydrants, electricity and the dump station are listed as available year-round; contact City Hall about conditions during freezing weather.'), read 2026-11-03
note: City of Adair park campground just north of I-80 Exit 76, immediately past the bridge on the east side; gravel pads, playground and ball fields. Bring a splitter for the water hookups. --Claude

name: Albert the Bull Park and Campground

season.note: Open from the 3rd week in April until the 3rd weekend in October.

season_source: https://www.cityofauduboniowa.com/c/-/?p=campground.html ('The campground is open from the 3rd week in April until the 3rd weekend in October.'), read 2026-11-03
note: City of Audubon park campground (1108 E Division St) beside the Albert the Bull statue, with a shelter house with fireplace and electricity; on the 21-mi T-Bone Trail, next to the pool, track and ballfields. --Claude

name: Big Sioux Recreation Area

season.note: Campgrounds open mid April to mid October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Sioux/Park/Big-Sioux-Recreation-Area/Facility/Eagle-View-Campground/Availability ('Campgrounds are open mid April through mid October'), read 2026-11-02
note: Sioux County Conservation park on the SW edge of Hawarden, on a 90-acre lake complex beside the Big Sioux River. Two campgrounds about 500 m apart: Eagle View on a peninsula with water on three sides, and Meadowlark on the lake's north shore. Swimming beach, boat ramp. --Claude

name: Clay County Fairgrounds

season.note: Non-fair camping April through October.

season_source: https://claycountyfair.com/plan-an-event/off-season-camping/ ('From April through October, the Clay County Fairgrounds offers approximately 15 acres of camping space'), read 2026-11-03
note: Camping on about 15 acres of open, gridded fields at the Clay County Fairgrounds in Spencer, open to travelers outside fair time. Pay after arriving, by phone or at the Events Center office (weekdays). Open campfires prohibited. Run by the Clay County Fair Association. --Claude

name: Sunnyside Park
season_source: note prose
note: City of Atlantic municipal park (Sunnyside Park, on the Cass County Fairgrounds grounds). ~20 defined electric/water RV pads (20/30/50 amp); reservable (not fair-only camping). Sanitary dump, restrooms with showers; in-town park with pool, ball fields, disc golf. Open ~Apr-Nov; drive-in back-in/pull pads fit a 23-ft rig. Nishnabotna River is well west and screened by fields, so sites are not on the water. --Claude

name: Swan Lake State Park

season.note: Open late April through mid/end of October, weather permitting.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/carroll/Park/Swan-Lake-State-Park (read 2026-11-04): 'The Swan Lake Campground is open late April through mid/end of October, weather permitting.'
note: Carroll County Conservation Board park (county-run despite the 'State Park' name). The campground sits on the lake's south side; the electric-only loops (A-P) run north through woods toward the fishing jetty. Reviewers report 28-35 ft rigs fitting (gravel, some grade; bring levelers). Hosts at sites 29 and 34, Memorial Day to Labor Day. Dump station $3 and showers $4 for non-registered visitors. --Claude

name: Wolden Recreation Area Campground

season.note: Mid April through mid October, weather permitting (MyCountyParks camping page; the park page says April through October). 2026: water and electric shut off by October 16; camping is allowed after that without them.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/Emmet/Park/Wolden-Recreation-Area-Campground/Activity/Camping (Hours: 'Mid April through mid October, weather permitting') + https://emmetcountyparks.com/visit-us/campgrounds/ ('all Emmet County campgrounds will have water and electric shut off by October 16th, 2026. Patrons are welcome to continue camping throughout the season, but will not have access to these amenities.'), read 2026-11-03
note: Emmet County Conservation park on 467-acre High Lake, 6 mi east of Wallingford, beside the Emmet County Nature Center and arboretum. The loops sit in woods behind a treeline along the shore; swimming at Pappy's Lakeside beach nearby. --Claude

name: Yellow Smoke Park

season.note: Open mid-April through October, weather permitting.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Crawford/Park/Yellow-Smoke-Park/Facility/Yellow-Smoke-Campground ('Open mid-April through October weather permitting'), read 2026-11-03
note: Crawford County Conservation park east of Denison on Yellow Smoke Lake (the county gives 37 and 40 acres). The 61-site main campground has gravel pads among trees along the lake's north shore; the 15-site North Campground sits up the hill with its own comfort station. On-site resident host. Cabins, a boat ramp, an accessible fishing pier and a 4-mile paved trail. --Claude

name: Bessman-Kemp Park
season_source: note prose
note: Hardin County Conservation park on 71 acres along the Iowa River, ~1/2 mi west of Alden, with 2 cabins and a shelter; no dump or showers. Open mid-April to mid-October, weather permitting. Carry-down river access for fishing/kayaking. Sites 2-4 sit along the river behind a fringe of bank trees; 10 and 11, near the cabins, look out on it. --Claude

name: Daisy Long Memorial Park

season.note: Campground season April - October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/hardin/Park/Daisy-Long-Memorial-Park-Bates-Addition/Facility/Daisy-Long-Cabin ('Park Hosts onsite at the campground during campground season (April - October)'), read 2026-11-02
note: Hardin County Conservation park on the Iowa River ~1 mi E of Union, site of the 1856 grist mill, with on-site camp hosts. The river-access boat ramp was posted 'currently in need of repair and unsafe for use' (read 2026-11-02). Sites accommodate ~25 ft, so a 23-ft Class C fits. --Claude

name: Dakins Lake Campground

season.note: April - October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Story/Park/Dakins-Lake ('Campground is open April - October'), read 2026-11-02
note: Story County Conservation, N of Zearing, on 20 acres of water in two lakes (electric trolling motors only; no swimming). Two campgrounds: the main loop with the shower house, and the east campground with its own entrance off 710th Ave. Main-loop sites overlook the lake across open grass but sit back from the waterline. --Claude

name: Featherstone Memorial Park

season.note: The county says the campground closes December through April (water and electric off); campers staying then still pay the nightly fee.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/Calhoun/Park/Featherstone-Memorial-Park ('The campground will close December through April. If staying through the times that the campground is closed (water or electrical turned off) you will still have to pay the normal fee per night.'), read 2026-11-03
note: Calhoun County Conservation Board park (51 acres) on the northwest shore of North Twin Lake near Manson, on the bike trail that circles the lake. The RV rows sit inland of the park's shore road, with a strip of lakeside cabins and trees between them and the water; sites A1-A30 at the south end are extended-stay. --Claude

name: Margaret MacNider Park Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Mason City municipal campground in Margaret MacNider Park on the Winnebago River, next to the city Aquatic Center, run by Mason City Parks and Recreation. Herringbone gravel pad rows in an open grove, set back from the river behind a riparian treeline, with a tornado shelter/bathhouse, picnic shelters and an office/camp store; the campground manager sells reduced-price pool passes. --Claude

name: Marion County Park Campground

season.note: Open from the second Friday in April to the last Sunday in October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Marion/Park/Marion-County-Park/Activity/Camping ('open seasonally from the Second Friday in April through the last Sunday in October'), read 2026-11-03
note: Marion County Conservation, SW edge of Knoxville (RV Life mis-tags it commercial; it is county-run). Gravel pad rows in open grass, shade moderate to limited, with an open picnic shelter and a campground host. Historic village on site. A ~3 ha fishing lake lies 130-150 m SW of the west pads across the park road and day-use lawn, not at the sites. Site water may be off in freezing weather (fill at the hydrant). --Claude

name: Pine Ridge Park
season_source: note prose
note: Hardin County Conservation park on the west bank of the Iowa River, NW of Steamboat Rock, with an 8-acre fishing lake about 350 m north through the woods. Season about April to September. The pads on imagery run about 14-20 m; the south and east pads sit 20-30 m from the river behind a band of bank trees, and a reviewer warns the campground can flood quickly when the river rises. A shooting range in the park can be heard by day. --Claude

name: Roberts Creek Park - East Campground

season.note: Open from the second Friday in April to the last Sunday in October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Marion/Park/Roberts-Creek-Park-East-Campground/Facility/East-Campsite-02 ('Closed seasonally from the last Sunday in October till the second Friday in April'), read 2026-11-02
note: Marion County Conservation park on the county's 300-acre Roberts Creek Lake, next to Lake Red Rock; county-run, not Army Corps. East campground is in two blocks, north and south of the entrance road, with a campground host. --Claude

name: Roberts Creek Park - West Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Marion County Conservation park on the county's 300-acre Roberts Creek Lake, next to Lake Red Rock; county-run, not Army Corps. West campground runs along a wooded ridge road with a campground host. --Claude

name: Wilkinson Pioneer Park

season.note: First weekend in May through the second weekend in October, weather permitting; the shower house may close in cold weather while the campground stays open.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/cerro-gordo/Park/Wilkinson-Pioneer-Park ('First weekend in May through second weekend in October depending on weather conditions.') + Site 01 page ('Shower house/restroom facilities may be closed while the campground remains open to prevent freezing.'), read 2026-11-03
note: Cerro Gordo County Conservation park at Rock Falls, on the Shell Rock River, with a covered bridge, native prairie remnants and a canoe launch. --Claude

name: Ackley Creek Park

season.note: Open approximately May through October, weather and conditions permitting.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Floyd/Park/Ackley-Creek-Park ('Open seasonally from approximately May through October, weather and conditions permitting.'), read 2026-11-03
note: Floyd County Conservation park of 40 wooded acres along Ackley Creek, a mile southwest of Marble Rock, with two shelters, a playground and hiking trails. The camping loop sits in the woods with no view of the creek or the Shell Rock River, which is about 350 m northeast across fields. --Claude

name: Eveland Access Campground

season.note: Opens the Friday of the 3rd full weekend in April, weather permitting; closes the last full weekend in October.

season_source: https://www.mahaskaconservation.com/cabins/eveland_access_campgrounds/ ('The campgrounds open the Friday of the 3rd full weekend in April (weather permitting) and close the last full weekend in October'), read 2026-11-02
note: Mahaska County Conservation Board campground on the Des Moines River SW of Beacon, in east and west sides, with a concrete boat ramp and two cabins next door. The east side's road runs along the sandy riverbank with the pads on its inland side. --Claude

name: Grundy County Lake

season.note: Closed during the winter months; dates not published.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Grundy/Park/Grundy-County-Lake-Park-Campground ('The campground is closed during the winter months'), read 2026-11-02
note: Grundy County Conservation Board campground at the SW corner of Dike, beside a former DOT borrow lake with a paved trail around it. The camp loop is separated from the lake by a wetland, tree plantation and park road, not on the water. --Claude

name: Halvorson Park

season.note: Open seasonally, early May to mid-October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Mitchell/Park/Halvorson-Park ('Open Seasonally early May to mid October.'), read 2026-11-03
note: Mitchell County Conservation Board's 10.6-acre park on the Cedar River, 1.5 mi S of St. Ansgar: non-designated sites on shaded lawn along the riverbank, with a swim beach, boat ramps and docks, and a handicap-accessible fishing pier. --Claude

name: Hannen Lake Park

season.note: Mid-April to the end of October.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Benton/Park/Hannen-Lake-Park ('Camping: Mid April - End of October'; 'Closed to Camping: November - Mid April'), read 2026-11-02
note: Benton County Conservation park on a man-made lake of about 40 acres, the first county-built lake in Iowa. Self-register at the kiosk within 1 hour of arrival. The east row runs along the shore behind a loop road; a few sites on the northwest cove have open grass to the water. Beach, boat ramp for electric motors only, kayak launch, rustic cabin. --Claude

name: Howard County Fairgrounds Campground

season.note: The fair says the campground is 'available to the public from May to October each year (weather depending)'; the county tourism listing says April to November.

season_source: https://mhcfair.com/visitors/ ('The Fairgrounds Campground is available to the public from May to October each year (weather depending).') + https://www.howard-county.com/business/howard-county-fairgrounds-campground ('available to the public from April to November each year'), read 2026-11-03
note: Fairgrounds campground on the west side of Cresco, open to the public outside fair weeks. --Claude

name: Osage Spring Park
season_source: note prose
note: City of Osage park on the Cedar River, with primitive camping on the wooded high ground above the river; toilets, and drinking water from the namesake spring. Minimal hookups; confirm electric on arrival. Open about April to November. The sites have not been confirmed at the waterline. --Claude

name: Rodgers Park

season.note: Camping from mid-April to the end of October; the gates and water are shut the rest of the year.

season_source: https://www.bentoncountyia.gov/conservation/rulesandpolicies/ ('Campgrounds and campground gates are open the middle of April to the end of October.') + https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/benton/park/Rodgers-Park ('Closed to Camping: November - Mid April'), read 2026-11-03
note: Benton County Conservation park, 207 acres just north of Vinton on 21-acre Rodgers Lake, reached by gravel. Two camping areas: the main one on the slope above the lake's west arm, and a small loop of about six sites on the east shore by the enclosed shelter. Beach, boat ramp (electric or non-motorized), kayak launch, fishing piers, nature center and 5+ miles of trails. --Claude

name: Bankston Park

season.note: Park open April through November, 6:30 am to 10:30 pm.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/County/Dubuque/Park/Bankston-Park (Operating Hours & Seasons: 'April through November 6:30 am until 10:30 pm'), read 2026-11-03
note: Dubuque County Conservation park near Holy Cross: 140 acres of wooded hillside sloping to a grassy meadow along the spring-fed, trout-stocked Middle Fork of the Little Maquoketa (Bankston Creek). Primitive sites in the open meadow and beside a small fishing pond, a restroom and algific talus slopes. Creek is behind a tree belt from the sites. --Claude

name: Coffins Grove Park

season.note: Delaware County campgrounds are usually open mid-April through mid-October; vehicle access is closed in late fall and winter.

season_source: https://delawarecounty.iowa.gov/conservation/conservation-parks/ ('facilities are closed to vehicle traffic and allow only walk-in access during the late fall and winter season. Campgrounds are usually open from mid-April through mid-October') + https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/Delaware/Park/Coffins-Grove-Park ('Parks with campgrounds are usually open from mid-April through mid-October'), read 2026-11-03
note: Delaware County Conservation Board park (22 acres of bur oak woods) 4 mi NW of Manchester on Early Stagecoach Rd. One gravel loop: the water/electric sites in a row along the east edge, electric-only sites inside the loop, primitive sites at its north end. Coffins Grove Creek runs through the woods north of the loop (stream fishing); the county warns it can flood into the park. Two picnic shelters, ball diamond, playground. --Claude

name: Fountain Springs Park

season.note: Delaware County: areas stay open all year but are closed to vehicles (walk-in only) in late fall and winter; campgrounds usually open mid-April to mid-October.

season_source: https://delawarecounty.iowa.gov/conservation/conservation-parks/ ('All recreation areas, parks, and natural areas remain open all year. However, facilities are closed to vehicle traffic and allow only walk-in access during the late fall and winter season. Campgrounds are usually open from mid-April through mid-October.'), read 2026-11-03
note: Delaware County Conservation's 239-acre park and wildlife area 2 mi NE of Greeley along the Elk Creek (Fountain Springs) trout stream, in a narrow wooded valley reached by gravel Oak Road; primitive camping only. The county warns the valley floods in heavy rain. Site locations and pad sizes not posted (2026-11-03). --Claude

name: Gilbertson Campground and Education Area
season_source: note prose
note: Fayette County Conservation campground in the 1,000-acre Gilbertson Park on the Turkey River just south of Elgin, linked by a paved bike trail to the Gilbertson Nature Center (petting zoo and nature center open Wednesday-Sunday, Memorial Day to Labor Day). A separate equestrian campground has primitive sites and hitching posts. --Claude

name: Hubinger Landing

season.note: Camping season Memorial Day to Labor Day. Off-season camping 'at some parks' Nov 1-Apr 1, no water, self-contained only.

season_source: http://cityofkeokuk.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Campground-Camping-Fees.pdf ('Camping Season Memorial Day to Labor Day') + http://cityofkeokuk.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Campground-Rules-Regulations.pdf ('Off-Season Camping'), read 2026-11-02
note: City of Keokuk paved lot at the boat launch on the Mississippi, beside the Southside Boat Club, which holds the restrooms and takes payment. Rail yard and a grain mill next door, so expect noise. Dump is at the city's Bank Street campground, posted closed until further notice for trail construction. Floods at high water. --Claude

name: Oakland Mills Park - South Shore

season.note: Mid-April through mid-October.

season_source: https://secure.rec1.com/IA/henry-county-conservation-department-ia/catalog (South Shore Site 10 and Site 28: 'Available mid-April through mid-October.'), read 2026-11-03
note: Henry County Conservation campground at Oakland Mills Park, on the south bank of the Skunk River by the historic Oakland Mills Bridge, with a playground and river fishing access. A swinging-bridge trail connects it to the Top-of-Hill area. The dump station is at the Water Works campground. The South Shore shower house was temporarily closed in 2026; Top of Hill's was open. --Claude

name: Oakland Mills Park - Water Works

season.note: Mid-April through mid-October.

season_source: https://secure.rec1.com/IA/henry-county-conservation-department-ia/catalog (each site: 'Available mid-April through mid-October.'), read 2026-11-03
note: Henry County Conservation Board campground in Oakland Mills Park, on the north shore of the Skunk River west of Franklin Avenue; boat ramp and the Ross Observation Tower over an 87-acre wetland. Resident host. --Claude

name: Scott County Park - Woodside Campground

season.note: Mid-April through mid-October, weather dependent.

season_source: https://www.scottcountyiowa.gov/conservation/scott-county-park/campgrounds/woodside-campground ('open mid-April through mid-October (weather dependent)'), read 2026-11-02
note: Scott County Conservation, Scott County Park near Eldridge (18850 270th St), one of the park's five campgrounds. Open grassy loop, no water adjacent. --Claude

name: Wapello Fairgrounds Park
season_source: note prose
note: City of Wapello camping area at its fairgrounds/rodeo grounds on the north side of town (not the Louisa County fair, which is in Columbus Junction). The city posts nothing about it online; its season, facilities and rate rest on directory listings only (checked 2026-11-03). --Claude

name: Scales Pointe Camping & Boating

season.note: Opens in mid-April.

season_source: https://scalespointe.com/about-camping/ ('Camping will be available in mid April'), read 2026-11-03
note: Campground and marina (formerly Jolly Rogers) on a point of Coralville Reservoir north of North Liberty, with leased boat slips and storage, a boat ramp, courtesy docks, a camp store and Bobbers Grill (full bar, live music on weekends). Many full-hookup sites, including the shoreline rows, are seasonal. --Claude

name: Shady Oaks RV Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Family-run campground under big bur oaks on the old Lincoln Highway west of Marshalltown, open since 1925 and billed as Iowa's oldest private campground; home of The Big Treehouse. Hosts take cash or check. --Claude

name: Windmill Ridge Campground

season.note: Operator's pages differ: 'Closed October - March' on the home page, 'Open April - October' beside the prices.

season_source: https://www.windmillridgecampground.com/ ('Closed October - March') + https://www.windmillridgecampground.com/contact ('Open April - October'), read 2026-11-02
note: Private campground in Kalona (Amish country). Swimming pool, small pond/boating, volleyball. Paid-admission bluegrass festival in July and a gospel sing in August on the grounds (2025 dates). --Claude

name: Bailey's Ford Park

season.note: Usually open mid-April through mid-October.

season_source: https://delawarecounty.iowa.gov/conservation/conservation-parks/ ('Campgrounds are usually open from mid-April through mid-October'), read 2026-11-02
note: Delaware County Conservation Board park (170 acres) 3 mi SE of Manchester on the Maquoketa River. Trout stream and river fishing; Maquoketa River Water Trail terminus. --Claude

name: Buffalo Shores

season.note: Late April to mid-October; the county gives no exact dates.

season_source: https://www.scottcountyiowa.gov/conservation/information/rules/camping ('Buffalo Shores is not open in the winter'; 'campground offices - Open late April through mid-October'), read 2026-11-02
note: Scott County Conservation recreation area on the Mississippi River downstream of Buffalo. Concrete patios; river sites along the front row. Free public beach and boat ramp. --Claude

name: Hidden River Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Private campground on the Cedar River, 7 miles from Tipton, reached through a housing development and down a long steep drive; call the host on entering. Shore fishing; boat ramp $5 per stay. Open ~Apr 15-Oct 15. --Claude

name: Little Bear Campground
season_source: https://www.facebook.com/LittleBearCampground/ (post, Sunday November 1, 2026: 'CLOSED FOR THE SEASON SEE YOU IN THE SPRING!'), read 2026-11-03
note: Family-run RV park with cabins, tent sites and a banquet hall right off I-80 Exit 259 at West Liberty, beside a truck stop with gas and a convenience store; swimming pool and playground. A handy interstate overnight stop. No website of its own (Facebook page only); book by phone, pay on arrival. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $40 a night in 2026 (RV Life and Campendium, May and October 2026 stays), $36 in 2025. --Claude

name: New Wine Park

season.note: Park open April through November; water and the modern shower/restroom building are off from about November 1 to May 1.

season_source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/dubuque/Park/New-Wine-Park ('Operation hours are 6:00 AM until 10:30 PM April through November.'; Closures text), read 2026-11-03
note: Dubuque County Conservation park on the North Fork Maquoketa River ~5 mi N of Dyersville: wooded, with more than two miles of nature trail (a winter bald eagle roost), ball fields, volleyball, playground and rentable pavilions; resident park attendant year-round. Public hunting in season. --Claude

name: Rodeo Park Campground

season.note: The RV Park is unavailable from two weeks before Labor Day through September 30 for events at the Tri-State Rodeo Arena (Rodeo Ticket Office 319-372-2550 for camping then). The city gives no opening or closing dates otherwise.

season_source: https://www.fortmadison-ia.com/454/Fort-Madison-Campgrounds ('RV PARK UNAVAILABILITY NOTICE: Due to scheduled events and activities at the Tri-State Rodeo Arena, the RV Park will be unavailable during the following dates: Two weeks prior to Labor Day through September 30'), read 2026-11-03
note: City of Fort Madison camping in Rodeo Park, two areas sharing one office phone: the RV Park (2103 303rd Ave), a loop of gravel pull-throughs in open grass just north of the Tri-State Rodeo arena, and the City Campground (2134 302nd Ave), electric and non-electric sites with a shower building. Disc golf, trails, dog park and shelters in the park. --Claude

name: Mirror Lake State Park - Cliffwood Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Cliffwood loop: 35 sites, ~29 with electric; open May-Oct. Many sites accommodate larger rigs. Reservable online. CAVEAT: tentatively closed in the reservation system ~Feb 1-early Aug 2026 for a road-construction project (per WI DNR) - verify before relying on it in 2026. --Claude Rechecked 2026-09-30: the Feb-Aug 2026 construction closure has passed with no newer notice. --Claude

name: Mirror Lake State Park - Bluewater Bay Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Bluewater Bay loop: 63 non-electric sites near the visitor center/beach; open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable online. (Not affected by the 2026 Cliffwood/Sandstone Ridge construction closure.) --Claude

name: Rocky Arbor State Park
season_source: note prose
note: 89 wooded sites on paved loops; ~18 sites with 30-amp electric, rest primitive. Showers, dump station. Open Memorial Day-Labor Day. Mix of reservable and FCFS; reservable online. --Claude

name: Mill Bluff State Park
season_source: note prose
note: 21-site rustic family campground; 6 sites with electric, 15 non-electric. Vault toilets, hand-pump water, dump station, no showers. Max RV length 40 ft. Reservable online (some FCFS availability). Open late May-September. --Claude

name: Hartman Creek State Park
season_source: note prose
note: 103-site family campground (separate from the park's horse/equestrian area); many sites have electric (15/30/50A), others non-electric. Flush toilets, showers, RV dump station. Reservable online. Family campground closed Dec 1-Apr 1. --Claude

name: Big Foot Beach State Park
season_source: note prose
note: ~100-site campground; the upper loop is drive-in RV (gravel pads) with 34 electric sites, remainder non-electric; lower sites are walk-to tent. No water/sewer hookups; dump station, showers. Reservable online. Open seasonally ~late April-mid-October. --Claude

name: Pinewoods Campground - Kettle Moraine State Forest (Southern Unit)
season_source: note prose
note: Family/RV drive-in campground in Kettle Moraine SF Southern Unit; 101 sites in 3 loops, no electric. Dump station, showers, flush + vault toilets. Reservable online (roughly mid-May to mid-Oct). Separate Group Camp on-site and a separate Horseriders' Campground near Palmyra. --Claude

name: Pike Lake Campground - Kettle Moraine State Forest (Pike Lake Unit)
season_source: note prose
note: Sunrise family campground in Kettle Moraine SF Pike Lake Unit; 32 sites (24 wooded, 8 open), 11 with electric. Open early April to third weekend of October. Reservable online; unreserved sites FCFS. Showers, flush toilets, dump station. The 3 backpack sites are a separate hike-in area. --Claude

name: Whitewater Lake Campground - Kettle Moraine State Forest (Southern Unit)
season_source: note prose
note: Family drive-in campground in Kettle Moraine SF Southern Unit; 63 wooded sites in East (600s) and West (700s) loops, only ~2 electric (ADA) sites. Vault toilets, no showers; dump station on site. Open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable online. Separate from the Horseriders' Campground and Hickory Woods Group Camp. --Claude

name: Harrington Beach State Park
season_source: note prose
note: 69-unit family campground (31 sites with electric, plus non-electric, 5 walk-in sites, group site, accessible cabin); modern showers/flush toilets, dump station. Reservable online. Paved roads suitable for large rigs. Open roughly May-Oct. --Claude

name: Sandy Beach Lake Campground - Northern Highland-American Legion State Forest
season_source: note prose
note: Rustic drive-in NHAL campground on the SE corner of Sandy Beach Lake; sites 1901-1933 (~30 drive-in back-in tent/RV, walk-to tent-only at 1914-1916). All non-electric; vault toilets, hand-pump water, boat launch, sand beach. Reservable online (no FCFS). Open ~late May-early Oct. WI State Park admission sticker required. --Claude

name: Big Lake Campground - Northern Highland-American Legion State Forest
season_source: note prose
note: Rustic drive-in family campground in NHAL, sites 1801-1870 (70 sites), all back-in, gravel spurs off paved campground road. No electricity; hand-pump water and vault toilets. Reservable online (no FCFS). Open ~late Apr-early Nov. WI State Park admission sticker required. --Claude

name: Eagle Cave Resort
season_source: note prose
note: Private resort by Wisconsin's largest onyx cave. 78 sites; water/electric (30-amp) and primitive/seasonal sites, dump station, showers, lodge with restaurant. Max RV ~35 ft so a 23-ft rig fits. Open Memorial Day-Labor Day (in-cave programs off-season). Reservable online and by phone. --Claude

name: Pine Harbor Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Private wooded campground at 7181 185th St near (not on) Lake Wissota. ~16-21 full-hookup RV sites (water + 20/30/50 amp), plus 5 extended-stay RV sites, 7 electric-only, primitive sites, cabins. Open ~May 1-mid-Oct. Reservable online + phone. Takes transient overnighters; 23-ft fits. --Claude

name: Rohr's Wilderness Tours
season_source: note prose
note: Paddling outfitter that also runs a real 47-site drive-in campground on the Wisconsin River headwaters, 5230 Razorback Rd, Conover. 25 full-hookup sites (30/50 amp, most pull-thru) plus a couple W/E sites and tent/walk-in sites. Drive-in RV pull-thrus fit a 23-ft rig. Opens ~mid-May; reservations by phone. Canoe/kayak rentals, disc golf, shower house, camp store. --Claude

name: Eagles Landing Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Standalone 45-site wooded RV park along the Yellow River, operated by St. Croix Casino Danbury (tribal-owned), just south of the casino - a real RV park with actual sites, not a casino parking lot. 35 full hookups (W/E/S, 50 amp) + 10 electric-only; big-rig friendly, max ~40 ft. Free showers, coin laundry, WiFi, shuttle to casino. Season ~late April-Oct 15. Reserve by phone or via casino. --Claude

name: Tom's Campground
season_source: note prose
note: 55-acre family campground ~35 mi W of Madison. ~96 sites (36 tent, 60 W/E, 12 electric-only), 16 pull-throughs, 30/50 amp; big-rig friendly. Dump station, showers, flush toilets, WiFi. Season ~April 15-Oct 31. CAVEAT: showed 'closed for the 2025 season' but takes phone reservations for the following year - verify 2026 operation by phone before relying on it. Reserve by phone/office (also Hipcamp). --Claude Rechecked 2026-09-30: site says open for the 2026 season. --Claude

name: Hi-Pines Campground
season_source: note prose
note: 75-acre wooded family campground ~1 mi N of downtown Eagle River at 1919 US-45 N. ~150 sites incl. 40 full hookups, 84 water/electric, 56 pull-throughs; 30/50 amp. 1-acre swim pond, water park, trails, ATV access, fiber WiFi. Season ~May 1-Oct 15. Reservable online (full payment at booking). Takes transient/overnight. --Claude

name: Happy Ours RV Park
season_source: note prose
note: 16-acre RV park at 14627 S East Mail Rd, Gordon WI with direct ATV trail access. 76 large sites, full water hookups + 30/50 amp; full-hookup sites and secluded tent sites. Open ~May 1-Sept 30. Big pull-through sites fit a 23-ft rig easily. RV Life geoloc was ~6 km off; corrected to the listed address. --Claude

name: Cedar Falls Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Utility-run (Wisconsin Valley Improvement Co.) campground at the Cedar Falls dam where the Tomahawk River meets the 7,000-acre Willow Flowage, Hazelhurst. 42 total sites, ~30 with electric (incl. rustic sites along the Tomahawk River); boat landing on site. Season ~late April-mid October; reservable online (advised >=1 day prior), walk-in not guaranteed; monthly rates for 30+ nights. Drive-in RV access. WVIC = utility operator, so ownership=private per criteria (like Brookfield/PPL). Year-round phone 715-848-2976. --Claude

name: Top O' The Morn Resort & Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Family-run lakeside resort on ~1,000 ft of Iron Lake shoreline in Bayfield County. 61 RV sites incl. full hookup, 30/50-amp, lakeside and pull-through; site descriptions say sites accommodate the biggest big rigs. 5 lakeside cabins. Open ~May 1-Oct 15. Reservable (own site/RoverPass). Easily fits a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Wildwood Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Small private RV-only campground (no tents) near Iron River. 25 sites, ~14 available for nightly/overnight (rest seasonal): 5 full-hookup and 19 electric+water, 30/50-amp; dump/limited sewer, swimming beach, boat/canoe/kayak rentals, playground, pavilion. Open May-Oct. Reserve by phone (715-372-4072) or email; not on a major online portal. Fits a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Borderline RV Park
season_source: note prose
note: Private RV park ~1.5 mi south of Land O' Lakes on US-45 along the Wisconsin River, on the WI/MI-UP border. ~30 sites, full hookups (30/50-amp electric, water, sewer), pull-throughs, big-rig friendly (23-ft no issue); WiFi, laundry, fish cleaning house. Open May-October; daily/weekly/monthly/seasonal rates, reserve by phone. --Claude

name: Devil's River Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Private campground at 16612 County Road R, Maribel, on the Devils River by the historic 1847 Rock Mill / mill falls. ~152 grassy sites with electric (30-amp) and water hookups; central dump station, laundry, showers, swimming pond. Sites rentable daily/nightly (~$30-$45) or seasonally; open seasonally. Reservations by phone (not online). Grassy sites fit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Central Wisconsin State Fair
season_source: note prose
note: Municipal fairgrounds park at 513 E 17th St, Marshfield, owned by the City of Marshfield (Marshfield Fairgrounds Commission); the fair is run by the Central Wisconsin State Fair Association. NOT event-only: operates a public campground for nightly/short-term RV camping ~May 1-Oct 18 (closed during the August fair and other reserved events). 100+ water/electric sites (30 & 50 amp) plus 500+ primitive spaces; dump station $5. Reserve via a Non-Fair-Time Camping Form / call ahead; no long-term camping. Flat fairground sites fit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Wildwood Haven Resort and Campground
season_source: note prose
note: On 111-acre Long Lake; W/E hookups 50/30/20 amp, sites 40+ ft long (23-ft rig fits easily), dump station, boat launch/docks/swim area, rentals. Open mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Kilby Lake Campground
season_source: note prose
note: On 50-acre no-wake Kilby Lake; ~124 wooded sites, full hookups 30/50-amp W/E/S, pull-throughs (23-ft rig fits easily), heated pool, restrooms/showers, laundry, boat launch, rentals. Open ~Apr 15-Oct 15. Reservable online + phone; seasonal sites exist but overnight offered. --Claude

name: Omro RV Park
season_source: note prose
note: Explicitly a transient (no-seasonal) in-town RV park; 30 electric-only pull-through sites all 80 ft long, 30 amp, dump station + fresh water, no sewer/full hookups. Open ~May 8-Oct 23. Regular nightly stays FCFS (14-day max); the 1-week-minimum/prepay rule applies only to EAA AirVenture week. No tents/pop-ups/vans. --Claude

name: Hickory Oaks Campground
season_source: note prose
note: 76 sites (29 W/E 20/30/50 amp, 48 no-hookup), pull-throughs available (23-ft rig fits), dump station, sandy swim beach on a private ~4-acre spring-fed lake. Adjacent grass airstrip but a normal vehicle drives in. Open ~May 1-mid-Oct. Reservations online only. --Claude

name: Deep Lake Campground
season_source: note prose
note: On Deep Lake (no-wake); RV sites, cabins, tent sites, plus year-round mobile-home spots; daily RV from ~$45/night. Open ~Apr 15/May 1-Oct 15/31. Daily bookable online; seasonal by phone. Leans seasonal but daily availability exists. --Claude

name: Christian's Campground
season_source: note prose
note: ~24 full-hookup + 1 W/E RV sites, packed-gravel pads on grass, remote/rural ~SW of Pelican Lake village, direct ATV-trail access, playground/horseshoes/volleyball. Open May-Oct; caters to seasonal but takes nightly (book by phone/email). Gravel pull-ins on a 24-site park should fit 23 ft. No standalone official website (strike) and near-zero independent reviews - moderate confidence; confirmed operating via RoverPass/Travel Wisconsin/Oneida County. --Claude

name: Alana Springs Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Private campground in the wooded hills of Richland County, est. 1955, WACO member. 35 sites, 30A electric + water (no sewer noted), 3 pull-throughs, listed big-rig friendly. Open ~Apr 1-Nov 30, nightly $22-$38. Seasonal residents hold most sites but transient/nightly sites bookable online. --Claude

name: White Tail Ridge Campground & RV Park
season_source: note prose
note: Wooded private campground ('Whitetail Ridge / Backwoods Saloon') deep in maple/aspen woods near Sarona, N753 Shallow Lake Rd. Water + electric hookups (sewer likely dump-station only), free showers, flush toilets, dump station, saloon/rec hall. Large weekend + seasonal sites; ATV/snowmobile trail access. Open ~Apr 1-Oct 1, nightly from $45. Online booking. Large wooded sites fit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Pine View Campground (Fort McCoy)
season_source: note prose
note: Fort McCoy Army MWR campground on Suukjak Sep Lake, open to the public (recreation area accessed off Hwy 21, no base credentials needed). 170 sites (~126 full-hookup W/E/S 30/50A, 12 electric-only, 32 tent) + 16 lakeside cabins; beach, fishing dock, dump station. Open ~May 1-Nov 30. Reservable via Army WebTrac + phone. --Claude

name: Terrace View Campsites
season_source: note prose
note: Rustic wooded private campground on spring-fed Muskellunge Lake (163 acres), Lincoln County. 45 sites: 3 full hookup, 38 water + 20/30amp electric, 4 electric-only (no 50amp). 32-ft max RV length (call ahead if over 30 ft) - 23-ft rig fits. Showers, flush toilets, free dump station, 5 fishing piers, beach. Open early spring through mid-Nov. Book online or by phone. --Claude

name: St. Croix Casino RV Park (Turtle Lake)
season_source: note prose
note: Standalone RV park at the St. Croix Casino Turtle Lake (tribal-casino operated), 100 Tamarack St. ~17-28 sites; W/E hookups (20/30/50 amp, $27/night), plus cheaper unhooked wooded/gravel sites and tent sites; dump station, showers, laundry, pool, 24-hr casino shuttle. Open ~May 1-Oct 31. Big-rig friendly (to 60 ft). Reservable by phone. --Claude

name: Scenic Ridge Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Mostly seasonal park but offers transient nightly RV sites in the back meadow/hill area (2-night weekend min). W/E on all nightly sites (20/30/50 amp), no sewer, dump station on site. 11 pull-throughs; max ~30 ft. Season ~mid-April to mid-October. Sandy swimming beach + boat launch on Whitewater Lake. --Claude

name: Point Bluff Camping Resort
season_source: note prose
note: Intimate riverside park (~25 sites) on the Wisconsin River; 20-amp electric at each site plus a central water source, no sewer. Takes full-size campers/RVs, gravel pads on front sites. Transient nightly reservations bookable online. On-site bar/restaurant, tube/canoe/kayak launch. Season ~late May to mid-September. 23-ft rig fits; confirm exact length on booking. --Claude

name: Arbor Vitae Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Family lake campground on Big Arbor Vitae Lake (~1,090 ac); ~109 sites incl. 77 full hookups, 12 electric-only, 6 electric+water, plus tent sites. Sites 26-100 ft; 23-ft rig fits with full hookups. Transient nightly reservations by phone (2-night weekend / 4-night holiday min). Season ~May 1 to Oct 15. Boat rentals, rental docks, lake access via Link Creek. --Claude

name: Holden Park Campground
season_source: note prose (cleaned out of the note 2026-10-13)
note: Pepin County park on 97-acre Silver Birch Lake just south of Arkansaw (N5362 County Rd N), with a boat ramp: sites 1-16 are standard and 17-20 premium.  Open mid-April through November.  Not rated on RV Life. --Claude

name: Avoca Lakeside Park & Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Village of Avoca municipal campground on Avoca Lake (a backwater/lake off the Wisconsin River). ~105 large, well-spaced sites; all 30-amp electric, 18 sites 50-amp; water at bath houses, dump station, boat ramp, swim beach. Nightly $30 (electric) / $35 (electric+water); seasonal sites also offered. Open ~Apr 15-Nov 30. Reservable by phone (608-532-6831 weekdays, 608-532-6188 after hours). Reviews report rigs up to ~25-30 ft fit; 23-ft EKKO is fine. --Claude

name: Bay City Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Village of Bay City municipal campground on Lake Pepin (Mississippi River). ~25 sites: 17 full-hookup, 8 electric-water (older listings say up to 44 full-hookup); sand beach, public boat launch, large dock, fish-cleaning, pavilion. Open ~Apr 15-Oct 15. Mix of seasonal and transient — daily ($45)/weekly ($300) reservations open Mar 1, monthly Feb 1; reservable sites 21-23, 34-38, 43-44. Genuinely takes overnight transients. --Claude

name: Dalrymple Park and Campground
season_source: note prose
note: City of Bayfield municipal campground 1 mi north of downtown on a wooded bluff above Lake Superior overlooking Madeline Island. 34 rustic tent/RV sites; 20/30-amp electric at most sites, no water/sewer hookups, potable water, vault toilets. $30/site, FCFS (no reservations). Open ~mid-May to mid-October. City recommends no RVs over 25 ft, so 23-ft EKKO fits. --Claude

name: Lakeview Park
season_source: note prose
note: Village of Cecil park on Shawano Lake. ~35-40 sites with electric and water hookups (20 amp per Campendium); showers, flush toilets, dump station, beach, boat ramp, dock rentals. Open May-Sep. Camp by season/month/week/day; reserve by phone (715-853-4180 in season, 715-745-4428 off-season). --Claude

name: Clear Lake Park
season_source: note prose
note: Village of Clear Lake 260-acre park on Clear Lake; three campgrounds — Main ($40) and Pine Point ($40, 7 W/E sites: 18-22 are 30 amp, 23-24 are 30/50 amp, RV/popup/tent) plus primitive Maple Knoll ($20). Showers, flush toilets, dump station, beach, boat ramp. Open May-Oct. Reserve via online request or Village Office (715-263-2157); untagged sites are FCFS self-register Fri noon-Sun. --Claude

name: Brown County Fairgrounds
season_source: note prose
note: Brown County Parks campground on the fairgrounds midway, 1500 Fort Howard Ave, De Pere. 46 W/E full-service sites, free dump station, showers/restrooms (campers only), boat launch, WiFi. FCFS, no reservations; ~$32/night ($70 during special events). Camping unavailable during the fair/scheduled events and seasonally closed (e.g. mid-Nov-Dec) -- check the county availability calendar before arrival. --Claude

name: Dorchester City Park
season_source: note prose
note: Village of Dorchester ~40-acre park off County Rd A & Park St. ~30-40 sites incl. full-hookup 50-amp pull-throughs plus W/E and primitive; flush toilets, showers, dump. On-site stocked fishing pond. Open ~May 1-Oct 15, FCFS (no online reservation; call camping contact). --Claude

name: Fond Du Lac County Fairgrounds
season_source: note prose
note: Fond du Lac County fairgrounds RV park, 20 full-hookup sites (water, sewer, 50/30-amp) north of the grandstand. Reservable online (3 days advance, 14-night max). NOT event-only -- open most of the year; camping closed only the Sunday-before through Friday-after the July county fair; water off ~mid-Oct to mid-Apr. --Claude

name: Waubedonia County Park
season_source: note prose
note: Ozaukee County's only camping park, ~40 acres on the east bank of the Milwaukee River in Fredonia (W1155 Fredonia Ave). 13 rustic campsites (some electric), $10/night, 3-night max; season 1st Sat in May through 3rd Sat in October. Reserve by phone. Boat launch, riverbank fishing. --Claude

name: Glen Hills County Park
season_source: note prose
note: St. Croix County park on 78-acre Glen Lake near Glenwood City. ~92 sites: Peninsula (55 electric, 20/30/50 amp, 2 cabins), Vista Prairie (35 water+electric), Picnic Point (10 non-electric, tent/truck-camper only), plus Whispering Oaks (12 extended-stay 30+ day RV). Season ~May 1-late Oct (off-season camping through Dec 31). Reservable online via Rec1. Dump station, showers, beach, boat landing. --Claude

name: White Mound County Park
season_source: note prose
note: Sauk County Parks & Rec park on White Mound Lake (a county-owned flowage/reservoir), S7995 White Mound Dr, Hillpoint. Family campground has 46 sites, 37 with electric, plus ADA, non-electric, and walk-in tent sites; shower building, coin laundry, vault toilets. Open ~Apr 1-Nov 30; reservable online (FareHarbor) and by phone. Separate 7-site equestrian campground and 3 hike-in rustic areas exist but the main family campground is drive-in RV. --Claude

name: Pine Point County Park
season_source: note prose
note: Chippewa County Facilities & Parks campground on a peninsula in 3,900-acre Lake Holcombe (Holcombe Flowage), ~2.5 mi W of Cty M / Hwy 27, Holcombe. 48 wooded sites, all with 20/30/50-amp electric; many sites directly on the water with some offering boat docks ($5/night dock fee). Beach, swim area, playground, pavilion. Open ~first week of May through last week of October; reservable online May-mid-Sept, FCFS self-registration mid-Sept-Oct. --Claude

name: Ledge Park
season_source: note prose
note: Dodge County park (83 ac) on the Niagara Escarpment overlooking Horicon Marsh. 41 sites: ~24 electric (20/30 amp) in lower loop + ~16 non-electric/primitive upper + 2 group; potable water fill, dump station, showers. Mostly back-in; only site 20 is electric pull-through. Reported max ~32 ft. Open ~Apr-Oct. Reservable online (Premier Campground). RV Life tags it commercial but operator is Dodge County (local government). --Claude

name: Moon Lake Park
season_source: note prose
note: Town of Iron River municipal campground on 41-acre Moon Lake (operated by the Town, not a city). North and South loops; electric on most sites, water in campground (not per-site), no sewer; sand beach, boat ramp, dump station, ATV-trail access. Season ~mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservations online. --Claude

name: Ravine Park Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Operated by the Village of Lake Nebagamon (Douglas County), at 11505 Camp Nebagamon Dr near the public boat landing at the lake's south end. 10 rustic sites (6 electric, 4 non-electric), flush toilets, no dump station; $30 electric / $15 tent, Memorial Day-Labor Day, FCFS via self-registration. --Claude

name: Columbia Park
season_source: note prose
note: Operated by Fond du Lac County (Planning & Parks) on Lake Winnebago / Calumet Harbor at N10340 Calumet Harbor Rd, Malone (~10 mi NE of Fond du Lac). 40-unit modern campground, all electric (20/30/50-amp), restrooms, RV/boat dump stations, marina/docking. Reservable online (~May-Oct). --Claude

name: Manitowoc County Expo Center
season_source: note prose
note: Manitowoc County Expo (county fairgrounds) at 4921 Expo Drive. Real overnight RV camping, not events-only: ~91 elec/water sites (Midway asphalt 54, North gravel 31, Vista grass 6). Water service May 1-Oct 15; camping May 1-Jul 31 and Sep 1-30 (grounds close Aug for county fair). FCFS, reservations not required; showers/restrooms. --Claude

name: Babcock County Park
season_source: note prose
note: Dane County Parks campground on the east side of Lake Waubesa at the Yahara River outflow, near McFarland off US-51. 25-unit campground, electric to all sites; bathhouse/showers, dump station, boat launch, fishing pier. Open ~late Apr-mid Oct. Reservable online or by phone. --Claude

name: Lake of the Falls County Park
season_source: note prose (cleaned out of the note 2026-10-13)
note: Iron County park on the Turtle River between Lake of the Falls and the Turtle-Flambeau Flowage, with a boat landing.  Three camping areas: the electric sites on Side 1, lakeside sites on Side 2, and showers and flush toilets on Side 3.  Open about May 1 to October 15. --Claude

name: Russell Memorial Park and Campground
season_source: note prose
note: Clark County park (NOT Jackson) on the shore of Lake Arbutus, W8180 South Rd, Merrillan; full-hookup (30-amp electric/water/sewer) plus electric-only and primitive sites, dump station, 3 shower houses, boat launch; RVs up to ~25 ft; reservable online May 1-Sep 30, season May-Nov, $24-37/night. --Claude

name: Totogatic Park
season_source: note prose
note: Washburn County park on the Minong Flowage, N13984 Tota Dr, Minong (~7 mi W of Minong); 105 sites, most electric (30/50-amp), some with water/sewer, nearly half with direct flowage access; sandy beach, boat ramp, showers, dump stations; all sites reservable online; season ~May 1-Nov 30. --Claude

name: Green County Fairgrounds
season_source: note prose
note: Green County Fairgrounds, 2600 10th St, Monroe; ~100 campsites, most with 30-amp electric and many with water; seasonal camping first Sat of May through last Sat of Sept (no camping during fair week in late July); FCFS self-registration (in-person office or drop box), $30/night. --Claude
